quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! They can also hover in mid-air by flapping their wings in a figure-eight pattern up to 80 times per second. The Pacific Northwest is home to the Rufous hummingbird, which migrates through Port Angeles each fall on its way to Mexico.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Sea Stars
short_read.teaser: Sea stars have no brain or blood, yet they can regenerate lost arms and even clone themselves. Discover the fascinating abilities of these colorful creatures that live right in the Strait of Juan de Fuca.

medium_read.title: The Beautiful Castles of Hungary
medium_read.teaser: From medieval fortresses to baroque palaces, Hungary's castles tell stories of kings, queens, and centuries of history. This photo journey explores some of the country's most stunning architectural treasures.

long_read.title: The Ancient Art of Hungarian Embroidery
long_read.teaser: For centuries, Hungarian women have passed down intricate embroidery traditions, each region with its own distinctive patterns and colors. This exploration reveals how these beautiful folk arts continue to thrive today.

port_angeles.title: Roosevelt Elk at Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: Early September is a wonderful time to spot Roosevelt elk at Hurricane Ridge as they begin their autumn rutting season. These majestic animals, named after President Theodore Roosevelt, can weigh up to 1,000 pounds and are often seen grazing in the meadows. Bring binoculars for the best viewing!

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Absolutely right, Barbara! That tiny heart works incredibly hard to power all that hovering and flying!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! The answer is 1,200 beats per minute — imagine how fast that little heart is working!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: The answer is 1,200 beats per minute! That's about 20 times faster than a human heart — amazing for such a tiny bird!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To support their super-fast metabolism and rapid wing beats, hummingbirds must eat about half their body weight in nectar each day. They visit hundreds of flowers daily and can remember every flower they've visited!

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful, Ildiko! Pillangó is indeed butterfly — such a lovely, musical word!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is pillangó! Madár means bird, virág means flower, and méhecske means little bee. Pillangó is such a beautiful word for butterfly!
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: The Hungarian language is unique in Europe, belonging to the Finno-Ugric family rather than the Indo-European family. This means Hungarian is more closely related to Finnish and Estonian than to neighboring languages like German or Romanian.

puzzle_3.question: What is the deepest part of the Strait of Juan de Fuca?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Exactly right! At 650 feet deep, the Strait has some surprisingly deep channels — deep enough to hide all sorts of marine life!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: The deepest part is actually 650 feet! That's deeper than a 60-story building is tall, and it creates important habitat for deep-water fish and marine mammals.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: The Strait of Juan de Fuca connects the Pacific Ocean to Puget Sound and is about 96 miles long. Its deep waters and strong currents create rich feeding grounds for orcas, gray whales, and countless seabirds.
